summary: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-105544 - .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
details: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. The VSTest artifact postprocessor can consume a forged `executionComplete.json` from another local user and execute attacker-controlled output handling. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/517 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-284 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The tables list affected versions of Microsoft.TestPlatform.CLI and their patched versions. The VSTest CLI is also bundled in the .NET SDK; SDK versions are listed separately below. Updating a separately installed CLI package does not replace the SDK-bundled test runner. Microsoft.TestPlatform.CLI is affected starting with 17.2.0-preview-20220301-01, including the first stable release, 17.2.0. The first .NET 11 general-availability SDK is fixed; its earlier preview and release-candidate SDKs require an update to 11.0.100. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check the version of Microsoft.TestPlatform.CLI used by your standalone VSTest installation. Run `dotnet --list-sdks` to list installed SDKs and `dotnet --version` from the project directory to identify the selected SDK, including any `global.json` selection. ### How do I fix the issue? For standalone VSTest CLI installations, replace Microsoft.TestPlatform.CLI with its patched version listed above. For releases without a same-line fix, use a compatible fixed servicing line listed above. Install a fixed SDK listed above and ensure test invocations select it. Updating a separately installed CLI package does not replace VSTest embedded in an older SDK. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the VSTest repository at https://github.com/microsoft/vstest. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind.
